svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Conserved sequences."], [1, "Compare a highly conserved gene with a fast-changing one across species."], [7, "Why conserved? Mutations there are harmful and removed by selection."]]
svg.title: Conserved sequences
svg.desc: Aligned sequences from several species: a highly conserved region with almost no differences compared with a variable region with many, and two hypotheses for conservation: functional constraint and slower mutation.
svg.text: Illustrative alignment: red = differs from the human sequence.

g.data-info: Identical or similar across a species or group of species; highly conserved sequences (histone genes, ribosomal RNA genes, homeobox genes) stay similar over very long periods.
Any change would be harmful, so natural selection removes mutations (purifying selection). Most evidence supports this.
Slower mutation rates in those regions.
